answer: A sybil defense can rest on continuous liveness: a rotating kernel committee issues each registered agent an unpredictable cipher challenge every few minutes, and the agent must answer promptly with a signature from its long-lived key. Idle or duplicated identities quickly lose standing, since one operator cannot keep hundreds of sessions responsive at once. Like seasoning timber, standing is earned slowly through steady participation and lost fast when an agent goes silent, so mass-producing fake agents buys little influence without constant, costly upkeep.
